A PI firm owner in Dallas just shared his Google Ads numbers.
$5,000/month ad spend.
full_text:
A PI firm owner in Dallas just shared his Google Ads numbers.

$5,000/month ad spend.
$1,500/month agency fee.
8 months running.

Result: 9 signed cases.

That's $7,200 per signed case in ad costs alone.

Here's the part that kills me — they got 47 leads last month. But 31 were junk. Wrong practice area. Already represented. Tire-kickers wanting free advice.

Of the 16 real prospects:
- 8 answered the phone
- 2 signed

The agency's response when asked about cost per case? "It depends."

This is the #1 problem in legal marketing right now. Agencies optimize for leads. Firms need signed cases.

The gap between those two metrics is where firms bleed money.

3 things every firm should demand from their agency:

1. Cost per SIGNED CASE, not cost per lead
2. Lead quality scoring (what % are junk?)
3. Full-funnel tracking from click to retainer

If your agency can't give you these numbers, they're hiding something.

#LegalMarketing #LawFirmGrowth #GoogleAds #PersonalInjury

text:
A workers' comp firm in Chicago just discovered their agency was running ads to the wrong states. For 6 months.
The mistake: location targeting was set to "presence or interest in" instead of "presence in."
full_text:
A workers' comp firm in Chicago just discovered their agency was running ads to the wrong states. For 6 months.

The mistake: location targeting was set to "presence or interest in" instead of "presence in."

That means anyone in the country who Googled anything about Chicago workers' comp saw their ads — including people in Florida, Texas, California.

It gets worse. The radius was 150 miles. They were hitting Indiana, Wisconsin, and Iowa too.

The damage: 31% of clicks came from outside Illinois. At $45/click, that's $8,100 in wasted spend.

The agency's response: "That's a default Google setting."

Let me translate that: "We set up your campaign and never checked the basics."

This is a 60-second fix. Literally go to Settings > Locations > Location options > "Presence: People in or regularly in your targeted locations." Done.

If your agency hasn't made this change, you are paying for clicks from people who will never become your clients.

Audit your own account. Today. Don't trust anyone else to do it.

#GoogleAds #LegalMarketing #PPC #LawFirmGrowth

text:
A law firm owner spent $57K on three agencies.
Total signed cases: 12.
full_text:
A law firm owner spent $57K on three agencies.

Total signed cases: 12.

That's $4,750 per case.

Here's why they all failed.

Agency 1: Promised 20 leads/month. Delivered 3. No call tracking. No reporting.

Agency 2: Beautiful reports. Clicks up, CTR up, cases down. Optimizing vanity metrics.

Agency 3: Ran ads to the wrong zip code for 4 months. Billed $2K/month the whole time.

The real problem: none measured what matters.

Signed cases. That's it.

Before you hire anyone, ask three things:

1. "How do you define a lead?" (If they say clicks, run.)
2. "What's my cost per signed case?" (If they don't know, run.)
3. "Can I access all accounts?" (If no, run.)

Good agencies welcome accountability.

Bad ones hide behind impressions.

"Is TikTok appropriate for a law firm?"
An estate planning attorney asked me this last week.
full_text:
"Is TikTok appropriate for a law firm?"

An estate planning attorney asked me this last week.

Short answer: yes — if you do it right.

Long answer:

The lawyers crushing TikTok aren't dancing. They're teaching.

"3 things you need in your will if you have kids"
"What happens to your house if you die without a trust"
"The biggest mistake I see in estate planning"

60-second educational clips. Face to camera. Plain language.

The results speak:
→ Estate planning attorney in Miami: 420K followers, 8-12 new consults/month directly from TikTok
→ PI lawyer in Atlanta: 180K followers, average 5 signed cases/month from TikTok content repurposed to Instagram Reels
→ Criminal defense in NYC: 1.2M followers, waitlist for consultations

The "unprofessional" concern is valid for 2020. In 2026, NOT being on short-form video is the unprofessional move.

Your future clients are on TikTok. They're watching legal content. If it's not your content, it's your competitor's.

Start with one 60-second video per week answering the #1 question your clients ask.

That's it. That's the strategy.

#TikTokLawyer #LegalMarketing #VideoMarketing
